stem: An 8-year-old boy with asthma has frequent symptoms and has just been discharged from PICU after a severe exacerbation. When he is not well, what reliever dose should be written in his Asthma Action Plan?
explanation: For a child with worsening asthma symptoms, an action plan typically increases the short-acting beta-agonist dose to 6-8 puffs every 3 hours, then escalates care if there is poor response or ongoing deterioration.
rationale: The item already has suitable options and one best answer. The scenario asks for the reliever dose when symptoms worsen, which corresponds to a stepped-up salbutamol regimen rather than the routine as-needed dose.

optionExplanations.A: This is a usual reliever dose, not the increased dose for when the child is unwell.
optionExplanations.B: This is the appropriate stepped-up reliever regimen for the 'not well' part of the action plan.
optionExplanations.C: This is too infrequent for an exacerbation action plan.
optionExplanations.D: This is an excessive dose and is not the standard action plan recommendation.
